title: Fragment-aware allocator and staged evictor with kernel hinting for prefills
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: As model usage diversifies we see many short-lived fragments splintering across KV storage, resulting in small, noncontiguous allocations that increase decode prefills and kernel misprediction. Existing LRU-like evictors cause high churn for low-cost interactive workloads and lead to back-to-back kernel context switches. This ticket proposes a fragment-aware allocator plus staged evictor that: 1) preserves small hot fragments via soft-coalescing windows; 2) attaches lightweight kernel-hint metadata to fragments to bias kernel selection without full recompile; and 3) stages eviction with a probation phase that allows micro-merge and deferred compaction to reduce decode stalls.
acceptance_criteria: New allocator reduces number of fragmented allocations per-host by >= 25% on synthetic short-turnover traces
Evictor probation phase reduces urgent decode-prefill events by >= 15% under 95th percentile load
Kernel-hint metadata is emitted in runtime metrics and is used by kernel selector to prefer compact kernels for coalesced fragments in >= 80% of matches
End-to-end 99th percentile decode latency improves by at least 8% on the targeted workload after rollout
Unit and integration tests covering allocation, probation eviction, and kernel-hint propagation are added and passing
design_notes:
High level:
- Allocation: introduce 'fragment bucket' allocator that groups allocations by expected token-turnover and contiguity score (histogram of recent touches). New allocations are tagged with a frag_class (tiny/short/long-lived) computed from a short history window. The allocator tries to place same-class fragments into contiguous micro-slabs to enable future coalescing.
- Kernel hints: each fragment carries a 2-bit kernel_hint field (compact | balanced | throughput | compatibility). Hints are heuristically assigned at allocation and updated on hot-paths when decode patterns change. Kernel selector uses hints as a soft-priority when considering kernel candidates.
- Eviction: replace immediate eviction with a three-stage eviction pipeline: candidate -> probation -> reclaim. During probation (configurable window), the system attempts micro-merge (if adjacent free or low-valued fragments) and deferred compaction. If probation expires, eviction proceeds.
- Prefill/decode scheduling: decode worker receives fragment metadata (frag_class and kernel_hint) and can schedule prefill waves in lanes prioritizing fragments with high contiguity to maximize KV cache hits.

Trade-offs considered:
- Added metadata footprint vs. reclaimed cost: we limit per-fragment hint metadata to 1 byte to avoid memory overhead.
- Complexity in allocator vs. potential fragmentation reduction: initial implementation uses simple histograms and thresholds to keep computational overhead small.
- Risk that micro-merge adds CPU cycles during probation; mitigate by limiting merge attempts per-second and opportunistically performing merges during low-utilization windows.
implementation_steps: Design fragment metadata layout and storage format (1 day)
Implement fragment bucket allocator and integration with existing slab allocator (3 days)
Add kernel_hint field propagation to allocation and decode paths (2 days)
Implement staged evictor with probation and micro-merge heuristics (3 days)
Expose metrics: fragment_count_by_class, kernel_hint_matches, probation_evictions, micro_merges (1 day)
Integrate kernel selector to prefer hinted kernels (2 days)
Add unit/integration tests and synthetic trace harness (2 days)
Run cluster perf experiments and iterate on thresholds (2-4 days)
rollout_plan:
Feature gated behind runtime flag 'fragment_eviction_v2'. Rollout steps:
1) Canary: enable flag on 5% of serving hosts for non-critical model traffic for 48 hours, monitor fragment metrics and decode latency.
2) Ramp: 25% for 72 hours, evaluate probation_evictions and micro_merge success rate.
3) Wide: 100% for batch-prefill-enabled clusters after automated thresholds met. If probation_evictions spike > 10% above baseline, rollback.
testing_plan:
Unit tests for: bucket allocation, kernel_hint serialization, probation lifecycle. Integration tests using synthetic traces:
- Short-turnover synthetic trace (many small requests, high churn)
- Mixed-turnover trace (combination of chat-like and long LTR requests)
Measure: fragment fragmentation ratio, prefill count per-request, decode latency p50/p95/p99.
Also include stress test to ensure micro-merge does not regress CPU by > 5% on median.
